utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before we continue with the examination of Witness M, I can announce that I received the English and the French version of the transcript of Tuesday, the 5th of February, page 3150 in English, and 3151 in French, where Mr. Piletta-Zanin has pointed out that on this last page, the second, fourth, fifth -- no, second, third, fourth, and fifth line, the French text is translated on page 3150, the last four lines, and there seems to be some imprecision in the translation. If I would say that details are not translated, I think it's not strong enough. Part of what has been said is not properly translated. I thank Mr. Piletta-Zanin for drawing our attention to it, especially since this Chamber will usually rely on the English version of the transcript, although we try to listen to the French text as well and, whenever possible, read the French text if there's any reason for that. I thank you very much for assisting the Chamber in this respect, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Is there anything else we have to discuss before we continue? Then, please, would you bring in the witness, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mrs. M. You can hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning. I'm saying good morning to you. I didn't say good morning yet to all the others in this courtroom, so good morning to everyone now. You are still bound, Mrs. M, you'll understand that, by the solemn declaration you gave last week in the beginning of your testimony. And the examination will now be continued by Mr. Mundis of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Mundis: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness M, can you tell the Trial Chamber about the injuries your son sustained while riding on the tram, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: When my son was injured, I was not aware of the type of injury; I just saw the blood. But a couple of minutes later, I realised that he had injuries on both his legs -- lower legs -- on the internal -- inside of the knee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take your son for any type of medical treatment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I took him immediately. We call it the emergency department, and that was closest for me, and that is where I took him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the medical staff there inform you as to the type of injuries that your son sustained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at first, but once they had cleaned the injury, they told me what it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that the witness be shown the document marked P3106.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Usher, would you please -- yes, yes, please proceed. Give the document to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness M, have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a certificate from the emergency clinic when my son was admitted there for treatment of his injury.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the date of this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date is the 19th of June, 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that date refresh your memory as to the date that your son was shot while riding on the tram?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness M, does your son to this day suffer any long-term effects from having been shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even from before that, living through the aggression and the shooting, he does have psychological problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness M, can you tell the Trial Chamber about another shooting incident that you witnessed from your apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I remember that incident very well. I happened to be at the window because it was a quiet morning. It was about 10.00 in the morning and, suddenly, shooting started, bursts of fire. Whether they were bullets of a larger calibre or not, I don't know, because I don't know much about weapons. In any event, they ricochetted from the asphalt, and there was a group of people in the street. They were going somewhere. They all laid down, and when the shooting stopped, a woman stayed behind, lying on the ground in the street. Later, they took her away in a car. However, the woman succumbed to her injuries, because there was a big pool of blood left where she had been lying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the approximate date when this incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean which year or what time of year?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you know the year and/or the season of the year, or perhaps the month of the year.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was towards the end of the summer, and I think it was in 1993, towards the end of the summer, end of August, because it was still warm; the weather was warm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness M.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mundis. Ms. Pilipovic, is the Defence ready to cross-examine Mrs. M?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mrs. M, questions will be put to you now by counsel for the Defence. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Ms. Pilipovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. M, good morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we broke, you told us about an incident that occurred, as you explained to us, in a tram. Could you please tell us, at which tram stop did you get onto the tram?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: At a tram stop called Skenderija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many passengers there were in the tram?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't too full of people. I didn't count the passengers. Most of the seats were taken, and there were a couple of people standing, and I was in the front part of the tram.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you and your son were facing in the direction of the movement of the tram, towards the east, towards Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not quite sure which side that is, but it is towards Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us when it was that you heard the shot, whether you actually heard a shot? What exactly did you hear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: A shot was heard, but by then, there was already panic in the tram. I clearly heard the shot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just then, was the tram stationary or was it moving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was moving.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from your fear for your son, did you feel or see anything particularly unusual in the tram?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please explain your question a little?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you told us that you were frightened when you saw your son bleeding, but was there any particular reaction on the part of the people that were with you in the tram?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everyone was scared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you feel any smell [as interpreted] in the tram?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: The smell of gunpowder, shall I put it, burning, gunpowder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much later could you smell the gunpowder? Could you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm really not able to say at what point I could smell the gunpowder, because my child was injured, and I paid no attention to anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before that critical day, how frequently did you travel by tram along the same route?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rarely, because the trams were not working regularly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to that particular event, when was the last time that you had taken a tram before that? Was it a week or a month?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe months, but I don't know. I mostly moved around on foot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which part of town do you live?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Novi Grad, Alipasino Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that there was a cease-fire just then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, how is it you know that there was a cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know because there was a public announcement to that effect. It was announced over the media.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, in relation to that event, how many days or weeks prior to that event was it announced on the media that there was a cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you that exactly, but not much before that. It wasn't a long period of time that was involved. It was a short period of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were able to follow the media?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, using batteries. We listened to the radio using batteries or an accumulator.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us who signed that cease-fire as you heard about it on the media?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid that is a political matter. I suppose the authorised people for that did that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us who those people are? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I no longer remember the names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us go back to the event in the tram. You told us that you went to the emergency clinic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before going to that emergency clinic, did you see the trace of the bullet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't look. That didn't interest me. All I was concerned about was reaching the clinic as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the examination-in-chief by my learned friend, you said that the bullet came from the direction of Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how is it you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: How I know that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. On the basis of what are you telling us now that the bullet came from Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see how else I could put it because from what other direction could it have come but from Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the period of 1993 -- you said that the armed conflict in Sarajevo started in 1992. In the period of 1992, 1993, and 1994, did you move around town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that you were listening to the media when that was possible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether, as you moved around town, you saw any soldiers in town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not with weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "not with weapons," what does a soldier mean for you when you said you saw a soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everyone was wearing a uniform, so I couldn't say who was a soldier and who was not, but I didn't see any carrying weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you learn from the media that in Sarajevo, the part of the town that you lived, in Alipasino Polje, that there were troops known as the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and that they were stationed in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there were troops, but they were not located in the part of town in which I lived. They didn't have any institution of their own there, nor a front line. They simply were not located there in the part of town in which I live.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you know that they were located somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the front lines, on the separation lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the place where you lived, in Alipasino Polje, or more specifically, your building, in which direction was the separation line in relation to your building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not close by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say it wasn't close by, it means it was somewhere there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not somewhere there. Further away. It was not close to my place of residence. The front line wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the closest front line in relation to your building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: About a couple of kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us which part of town that is, or street, in relation to your area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Stup neighbourhood. I know that there was a separation line over there. Then Zabrdje, the neighbourhood of Zabrdje. That was what was relatively close to where I lived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that part of town, in the part of town in which you lived, were there any armed operations, let's say in Stup and the part of town in which you lived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the part of town in which I lived, you mean clashes between warring parties or sniper fire?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I mean clashes between warring parties.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my part of town, no. I'm repeating that. Maybe further away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you told us that the front line was a couple of kilometres away from your house. When you say "a couple of kilometres," what exactly do you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I knew more exactly, I'd tell you. But a couple of kilometres. The closest was less than 10 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which military formation was at Stup?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I tell you that Stup was under the control of the HVO, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would be unable to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us about this second incident, that there was shooting.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the building in which you live, can you tell us from what direction the shooting came? Did you see that at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the direction of the bullets hitting the street, which means that they were coming from Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are telling us now that it is possible to see Trebevic from where your building is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many kilometres Trebevic is from your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the crow flies, I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is it by road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me tell you it's 40 kilometres from your building. Would you agree with me? Maybe even 50.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about as the crow flies? [Realtime transcript read in error "A. Because the bullet flies directly through the air; it doesn't follow the road."] Because the bullet flies directly through the air; it doesn't follow the road. Can you tell us which part of Trebevic can you see from your apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you which part of Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many floors does your building have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which floor did you live on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: The eighth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the shooting started, where were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you at the window, looking out, or were you sitting in your room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at the window, looking out, because I didn't expect any shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that just then a woman was killed on that occasion. Can you tell us what the name of that woman is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm unable to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who you learnt about it from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the people who were there and who said that she was dead, who later recounted the event.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said "later recounted --"

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean during the day, during that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that any of the people you talked to reported that incident to the competent authority?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which competent authority. I hear that for the first time, that one could report these things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any one of you go to the police and report the incident and tell them about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm not aware that such incidents could be reported.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of the UNPROFOR officials on the spot, though they were in Sarajevo at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the people you spoke to, did you learn where that woman lived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: She also lived at Alipasino Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The incident that occurred when your son was injured, can you tell us whether you or any of those present reported the incident to the competent authorities? When I say "competent authorities," I mean the police.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't report anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of anyone else among the people who were with you in the tram reporting the event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness, when telling us about the incident in the tram and reporting the incident, told us today that she didn't report the incident and that she doesn't know of anyone else having done so, any of the other people present in the tram, and with your permission, Your Honour, I will show the witness a statement she gave to the investigators of the Tribunal on the 30th [as interpreted] of November, 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember making that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you signed that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the benefit of my learned friends and Your Honours, it is the statement of the 13th of November, 1995, number -- in the B/C/S version, on page 1, paragraph 4. With your permission, the witness [as interpreted] would like to show the witness what she said in that statement with respect to reporting of that incident which occurred on the day when, according to the testimony of this witness, her son was injured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, would you please read it for the sake of the transcript, because if the witness just reads it, we'll not know exactly what she reads.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. I will read the fourth paragraph, which begins with the words, "On the third stop..." "On the third stop, there were BH soldiers and UNPROFOR soldiers. This was at Pofalici. At this time, I was pregnant."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. M, did you make this statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain for us which soldiers of the BH army and UNPROFOR were there, and how many of them were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that there were BH soldiers. I said UNPROFOR soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. M, I've just read out what you said: "On the third stop, there were soldiers of the BH and UNPROFOR. This was at Pofalici." You said that that was what you stated. Could you tell us now which is the truth; what you're telling us now or what you said in this statement? When were you telling the truth; today, when you're telling us about the incident, or when you were making this statement? Will you please tell us which is correct.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that there were BH soldiers together with UNPROFOR soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're saying that what you stated in this statement is not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not claiming that it is not correct. I just don't remember that there were BH soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling us now that this is incorrectly noted down in this statement which you signed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not saying anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you made this statement to the investigators, did you read it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sign it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us today which is correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably that is more correct, because, after all, now it is the year 2002, and that was in 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what you're telling us is that your memory was fresher in 1995 of the event, regarding the event? Now, can you tell us now how many BH soldiers there were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: If any, very few; two or three perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether any of the soldiers of the BH army or UNPROFOR talked to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one talked to me. Immediately, with my husband's sister, went to the emergency clinic. I did not stay, linger on there at Pofalici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the members of the BH army and the members of UNPROFOR had inspected the tram and noted -- actually took statements from other people in the tram?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't take any statements from me. I didn't know what was going on because I had left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know whether the other passengers in the tram talked to the soldiers of the BH army or UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that because I left the premises.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you told us, the soldiers of the BH army were there. Since you said that they were not wearing uniforms, on the basis of what did you conclude that these were soldiers of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, would you please allow me to intervene at this moment. My attention was drawn by one of my colleagues that there might be a difference in the French and the English transcript, especially in relation to this specific point. And I would have left it for a later moment, but since it's part of your questioning now, as far as I see, the French version says that no one was wearing a uniform, while the English version says that everyone was wearing a uniform. So Mrs. M, we have some problems. We do not understand your own language, so we have to rely upon translations. And we see that we have two different translations. A question was put to you in an earlier stage whether you saw any military people; and then while answering and while explaining, you said, according to the one translation, that everyone was wearing a uniform and, in the other translation, it says that the no one was wearing a uniform. Could you please clarify this for us, which was the right translation? It was when you said about no military people ever carrying a weapon, and then the question was but how would you know that these were military people? Did you say, "No one was wearing a uniform," or, "Everyone was wearing a uniform"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, most of them were not wearing uniforms, especially at the beginning. No one had a uniform. Perhaps some people that I don't know had uniforms. But the people I knew were not wearing uniforms. In town, I couldn't see a male person wearing a uniform, if you understand me well. As far as military persons are concerned, if it were a patrol or something, they were wearing some kind of uniform just to be recognised as a military person. Perhaps -- have I managed to clarify this point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's a clarification. And it's also, Ms. Pilipovic, the basis of your question that I would say people were not wearing uniforms is the correct one. But I had to clarify it since there was this difference in the translation. Also, for the transcript's sake, this is at -- in the provisional transcript at page 8, line 16. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you would like to add something?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I wanted to say that Ms. Pilipovic was about to ask the question and to clarify this. We noted at 9.44.54, and this is what in fact was said. And this is -- for the transcript, I think that the situation is now clear. So this is the answer. 9.44.54, that was the answer that was given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your assistance. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. M, can you please describe how these people were dressed, the people you say were members of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. Can you imagine that I was really not in a situation to observe how people were being dressed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree that they had uniforms, because you said they were soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think they were wearing uniforms. I don't know if they were military or any other kind of uniform. I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you spoke of that other incident, can you tell us, you actually said that there was shooting in bursts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear any other sounds besides the shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many people at that moment were at that point, at that place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: About ten people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Observing them from the eighth floor, could you discern whether they were men or both men and women?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both; it was a mixed group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to see how those people were dressed, specifically both in relation to the men and women?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both were wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you say that some of those men was a soldier since you talked with them in that afternoon, as you described to us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't speak to everyone. This person was an elderly person, and he wasn't soldier. He told me that the woman was dead.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just a moment to consult with my colleague.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have concluded our cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Pilipovic. Mr. Mundis, any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Just one very brief line of questioning, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please. Re-examined by Mr. Mundis:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness M, do you recall the approximate distance from the location where the tram received the gunfire to the stop at Pofalici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in kilometres? Well, there were two stations, two stops between these two. There were two stations. One was called Museum, and the second one was the Marsal Tito barracks. So the tram didn't stop at those two stops but stopped at Pofalici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know approximately how many kilometres it is from where the tram was hit by the gunfire to the Pofalici stop?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't even say that even today. I could say 3, I could say 6 kilometres. I don't know how many. This can be established from -- I just wanted to point out that we didn't stop from that place to Pofalici. But as far as kilometres are concerned, I can say perhaps 4 kilometres. It may have been 3. I don't really know the exact number of kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness M.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mundis. Judge Nieto-Navia has one or more questions to you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Looking at the medical report, it says that the patient was injured with a dumdum bullet. The question is: The doctors, or somebody, told you what is a dumdum bullet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: The doctor didn't tell me what it was, but I heard what a dumdum bullet was and that it was prohibited, that its use was prohibited because it had vast destructive power. This is what I found out about the dumdum bullets. But the doctor at that time didn't tell me anything about it, but those who saw my son's injury, they said that it was probably that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. kind of a bullet involved, because his knees were full of small pieces of gunpowder. And now he also, even today, has small spots below his knee that are still visible even today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have not a specific question, but I'd like to ask a clarification to Ms. Pilipovic. Ms. Pilipovic, just in order to avoid any thorough misunderstanding, one of your questions was whether the tram was heading to Ilidza in an easterly direction. Are we talking about another incident or -- since what I learned from the incident now, everything tells me that the tram was heading west. And the witness did not say it was direction Ilidza. I don't know whether it's east or west. But it's just in order to avoid any misunderstanding between the Defence and the Bench.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the tram surely went in the direction of Ilidza, that is, the west side, the west direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Pilipovic. Mrs. M, thank you very much for coming a very long way from Sarajevo to The Hague. We are aware that it's quite a long way, and it's not easy perhaps -- it might not have been easy for you either to -- being confronted again with events in the past that certainly are of great emotional meaning to you. You understand that this Court -- that it's very important for this Court to hear the testimony of those who have been present at the time when a lot of things have happened in Sarajevo, and for the decisions for us to take, it's very important that people come and testify in this Court. So thank you very much for having taken the effort to come to The Hague. Thank you very much for answering all the questions of the parties, of the Judges, and I wish you a good trip home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please lead the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Madam Registrar, we still have to take the decisions on the admission into evidence of the documents tendered by the parties. Could you please guide us.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The pseudonym sheet will be P3652, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As far as I remember, we have admitted it already into evidence right away, according to our -- what we usually do. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And the medical document, P3106 for B/C/S and P3106.1 for English, both under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. All the other documents that have been used were already admitted into evidence when the first witness on this incident has been testifying. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although this is not the usual time to have a break, the Chamber finds reasons to have the break a bit earlier, and then we'll resume also at an earlier moment. That means 10 minutes to 11.00. So we have now a half-hour break before the next witness will be called. So we'll adjourn until 10 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we resume, Mr. Ierace, I expect that Mr. Lesic will be the next witness to be called. Before we ask him to be brought into the courtroom, I'd just like to say a few words on something that happened on the 6th of February at the end of the testimony of Mrs. Taric. As you may remember, I then noticed for, I would say, one or two seconds there was something on the screen which was not ordered to be on the screen at that moment. And I urged that whoever was at the technical booth not to show any images on any screen unless it has been ordered by the Trial Chamber or has been agreed upon by the Trial Chamber, that it was asked by one of the parties. I paid attention to it. I thought that it was necessary to get the information from the technical booth. I also found out it was made by mistake. I noticed that it cannot be of any influence on the testimony of that witness because the testimony had ended already when it happened. As a result of my request to find out what happened exactly, you may have seen that on the next day, the person who was moving the pictures of the 360-degrees photographs was in the courtroom instead of in the technical booth, which indicated clearly that it was done under the responsibility of the Office of the Prosecutor. So that's the measure that has been taken. Apart from that, I felt that I would be better in control. Finally, the reason why I'm telling it now is that this mistake was done by -- at that moment, it was Mr. Lesic, as far as I know, who was at the computer at that time. So just for the openness and for the sake of clarity, I think it would be best to tell the parties about what I did and what the result is. So, then, Mr. Ierace, please call your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just before I call Zoran Lesic, I inform the Trial Chamber that I have spoken with the Defence, and I understand there is no objection to Mr. Lesic's statement being tendered. I will ask him a few additional questions to cover essentially the manner in which the photographic images were transferred into an electronic form, and ultimately into the 360-degree photographs. Mr. Lesic is fluent in English as well as Bosnian, and I propose that he give his evidence in English. Thank you. I call Zoran Lesic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think Mr. Piletta-Zanin first wants to make an observation. Please do so, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Thank you for giving me the floor. But things are never quite as simple as presented by the Prosecution. First of all, Mr. Lesic, if I understand, is an assistant of the Prosecution, and this should be underlined. Secondly, we do not accept as such that he be considered as a usual expert because we have somebody who is a party. So how are we going to qualify him? He is an assistant of the Prosecution. That is one point. And secondly, this person, if he should be heard as a witness, I don't quite know what his status will be. He assisted in the courtroom or in the booth with regard to these 360-degree photographs. The reason why we wish to hear Mr. Lesic is primarily to draw attention of the parties and your Chamber to the very great difficulties that we have to manage this kind of procedure. And proof of that is the incident you, yourself, referred to, Mr. President, which happened spontaneously and which results from the technical difficulties involved. And we feel it is dangerous to use these photographs. They are useless and ineffective, and they can cause confusion. With respect to Mr. Lesic, we would like to know in what capacity he will be heard. And the thesis of the Defence would be to reject all the computerised 360-degrees photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, may I just ask you one question: If you say he's not a usual witness, that's fine, but what should be the consequence of not being a usual witness, in your view?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, you said yourself that this was a mixture of the Anglo-Saxon and continental procedures. What I wish to say, that if we listen to him as a witness who has taken an oath, he is a party paid by the Prosecution. So we are dealing with an employee of the Prosecution, and consequently, according to my legal tradition, and probably yours too, we are very suspicious of this kind of situation, for obvious, objective reasons. That's all I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... he is employed by the Office of the Prosecutor that we have to be very cautious in our judgement on what the probative value of his testimony may be. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me be clearer. It is all the more serious because if his exhibits are unacceptable, he may find himself being unemployed. So there is quite a serious problem there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Ierace, we are at the point where you could call Mr. Lesic, your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. I call Zoran Lesic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Lesic. You can hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We were informed by the Prosecutor's office that you speak English fluently and that you therefore choose to testify in English rather than in your native language. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then would you please first make the solemn declaration the Rules require you to make, the text of which will be given to you now by the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lesic, please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Examined by Mr. Ierace:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your name Zoran Lesic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes, my name is Zoran Lesic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 21st of November, 2001, did you make a statement to an investigator of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask that the witness be shown that statement, which is Exhibit P3653. I have a copy here at the bar table, together with additional copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand, Mr. Ierace, that you intend to tender this document into evidence, and I also do understand that there's no objection from the Defence side, of course, against the whole procedure of the 360 degrees, but not against tendering this document into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'm grateful to the Defence, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise on the document in front of you your signature?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that appears on every page of the document. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is what you said in the document before you, that is, your statement, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the truth?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Completely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. On page 1 -- I'm sorry. On page 2 of the statement, you set out your experience. Have you done any tertiary study, that is, study at university?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what institution was that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: It was university for drama. Original name is Fakultet Dramskih Umijetnosti.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what city is that institution?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: That was in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. When did you finish that course of study?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did that --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Sorry. 1976.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Also on page 2 of your statement, you set out in summary form the manner in which you took certain photographs. You say that you took those photographs between the 9th of September, 2001 and the 2nd of October, 2001. Were there any photographs taken after the date of the 2nd of October, 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: It was only one that, together with the investigator from ICTY, Barry Hogan, I took on the 18th of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Sorry; same year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Does that also relate to one of the scheduled incidents to the indictment?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, having taken the photographs and had the films developed, did you load the photographic images electronically into a computer?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that involve scanning the photographs or the negatives or both?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Scanning the negatives and positives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of equipment did you use for that scanning process?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: We use a Nikon film scanner, and the name is Supercoolscan 4000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it you then needed some software.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I notice Mr. Piletta-Zanin is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please. Using the same language, that's always the problem. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, the words spoken by Mr. Piletta-Zanin were not translated. But --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin asked on behalf of the French booth whether Mr. Ierace could slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now you got the message, Mr. Ierace. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you use some software in order to join the photographs Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. electronically?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the name of that software?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: We use a software called Ulidcool 360.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you joined the photographs so as to produce a 360-degree image, did you alter in any way the content of the individual photographs?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't. And that's also visible from some 360 images that part of them are lighter, part of them are darker. And that's how scanners scan them, and we didn't do any correction in anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, in relation to incident 24, which I shall refer to as the "tram incident," were you able to place the tripod over the spot earlier indicated by the relevant witness?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: No, because of traffic conditions. It was extremely busy day, which is visible on the video. And local police didn't want to assist us for stopping complete traffic to put the tripod in the same spot. In the same time, it was working in that area, and we were forced to do that three days later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean three days after the video was filmed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Three days after video.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the video, one can see some yellow marks being made by the investigator on the road surface. They do not appear on the 360-degree photograph. Do you know why that is?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: I think so. It was a construction works on the road the day when we filmed the video, and it was a very heavy raining day after that. Probably they cleaned the road when they repair the hole on the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you a question in relation to another incident in respect of which there has already been some evidence. That's scheduled sniping incident number 9 involving Vildana Kapur, who the Prosecution alleges was shot and wounded in her left leg whilst transporting water. Mr. Lesic, in relation to that incident, we have seen some photographs taken of the witness Ifeta Sahic. Do you know who took those photographs?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Just one question: You said number 9. Here on the list it is number 8. I know what case you are talking about, but just to make everything clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'm asking you about incident number 9. That's the amended schedule of sniping incidents. The Prosecution case is that three young women were walking along a road, transporting some water, when there was a burst of gunfire.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know that case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In that -- during the course of evidence in relation to that incident, there have been some photographs tendered showing Ifeta Sahic standing on a road. Do you know who took those photographs?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I made those photographs on a mission before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have also seen some 360-degree photographs taken from that area. One appears to have been taken from the road, and the other from a grassy area to the side of the road. Did you take those images?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how long before you took those 360-degree photographs did you take the photographs of Ifeta Sahic standing on the road, approximately?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Approximately a year ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, looking at your statement, at the bottom of page 2, have you produced some details from your log book?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are these the same details, that is, the details in bold, except for the first entry, being the date of the alleged incident, which appear at the beginning of each video clip?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By way of explanation, referring to incident number 1, the first detail which appears on the video is "17 September 2001 - 09h [TH 180cm]." What does the date refer to, 17 September 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: That's the date when we met the witness and when we made the video and photography.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: That's the time.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: That's the height of the photo camera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean height from ground level?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Height from ground level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To what part of the camera?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: The lens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Next line is "GPS*T34 - 0290137 - 4859181." What does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: That is a GPS reading done by investigator on that moment, showing exact position according to GPS reader.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that reading filmed through the videocamera?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes. The GPS reader was shown to camera, and camera was basically filming also the same details which are written here in the log book.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going over the page, the next line reads "Compas*E611m/S174." What does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: That is direction of videocamera. The videocamera was point in that direction, and that was also filmed on the videotape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On some of the footage we have seen so far, there appears to be two videocameras recording at the same time. Does the compass reading relate to the videocamera before which the compass reading is held up to the lens?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes. The first reading is for the first camera, and the second reading is for a second camera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, in relation to the next line, which reads "CAM1 tape 3 - 0:32:48" followed by an arrow, "0:37:32," what does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: That's a reading of time code from the videocameras. The first one is camera 1. That was tape 3 of that camera. And the beginning of that filming was on 0 hours, 32 minutes, 48 seconds. And it stopped on 0 hours, 37 minutes, and 32 seconds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please slow down your answer, especially when you're quoting figures.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having regard to your answer, I take it the second part of that line provides the same relevant details for the second camera; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The next line reads, "film ERN 0211-9720." I take it that is the ERN number that was ascribed to a film.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: That is correct. That is ERN number described [sic] for a photo film.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the photo film from which the 360-degree view was produced; is that the case?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you edited the video film, we have noticed some gaps and breaks. Firstly, as you've pointed out, there were two cameras used for some incidents. Are those gaps partly explained by, during the editing process, you switching from the film of one camera to the film of the other camera?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: No. The gaps that appear are GPS readings mainly, or naming the persons present, or from time to time we were shooting on location which was very noisy, like traffic control, and if there was like a couple of seconds, minutes, of hard noise of, let's say, truck passing by, we will stop filming -- we will film, but we will not show that in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you also switch from the film of one camera to the film of the other camera --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- in the final -- please wait for the question -- in the final presentation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes. We switched from one camera to other camera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you prepared the electronic photographs, on what did you mount them; in other words, on a computer hard drive, a separate hard drive, a CD, a DVD, or a videotape, or what?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: After finishing on the hard drive, we will export everything on the CD.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. When you say, "We will export everything on the CD," has that been done?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. No further questions in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the Defence ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Thank you. May I proceed? Thank you. Cross-examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, thank you for coming to explain to us what you know in this courtroom. I should like to go back to the document submitted by the Prosecution, which has now been prenumbered 2130748, and that is your written statement dated the 21st of November, 2001. You have confirmed signing this document, and it is on that basis that I have a few questions for you now. On page 2, you have indicated in your brief C.V. having worked in Sarajevo. Could you tell us, sir, during which period of time exactly you first studied and then worked in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was studying from 1972 until 1976, and from that moment I joined a chamber theatre, or Kamerni Teatar Pedesetpet, in Sarajevo, and I was working in that theatre until end of February 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if I understood you correctly, you lived for some 20 years in Sarajevo, or, to be quite precise, for 17 years. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: No. I was living even longer than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then that is my question. For how long did you live in Sarajevo, maybe studying before the university? Generally speaking, how long did you live in Sarajevo for?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: My family arrived to Sarajevo in '68, 1968.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So for some 25 years, you continuously lived in Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Witness, you perhaps had the opportunity to do your military service in Sarajevo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During those 25 years, you met a certain number of people. Among your circle of friends or acquaintances, did you know people who were militarily active in Sarajevo during the period we're interested in, that is, May 1992 until the end of 1994?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you lived in Sarajevo for 25 years. Did you also have among your circle people who, unfortunately, disappeared in Sarajevo during the period that I have just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Witness, among those people who went missing, were there people who disappeared as a result of violent death?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, we know that. Thank you for your answer. Were there people who you knew who died not only as a result of violent death but during -- as a result of a shot or as a result of combat?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. I understand your difficulty. Did you have close friends who disappeared under those circumstances in Sarajevo or the surroundings of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness, for your answers, which are clear, and I think important. On the first page of your statement, you indicated, with regard to your ethnicity - I think that's what we can call it - that your ethnic origin is Bosniak. Is that correct? I'm referring to page 1, the cover page of your statement which has just been shown to you and the last numbers of which are 748.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. It's my ethnic origin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, if I look at your place of birth, I see Zrenjanin FRY, which means the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. So this is Vojvodina, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you say that your ethnic origin is Bosniak, that means that part of your family are of Bosniak ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During these discussions, we have seen that there are several ethnicities in Bosnia. Could you specify, please, if possible, which member of your family belongs to the Bosniak ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes. My mother, she is a Bosnian Serb, and my father was a Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A Croat from Croatia or a Croat from Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Bosnian Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I come back now to the technical problems. You mentioned GPS. I think you're referring to the global positioning system; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Generally speaking, this system, as far as I understand, functions thanks to the assistance of a satellite; is that correct? What information can you give us regarding the GPS used, number 1; and number 2, the satellite on the basis of which it operated?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: As I know, it was a GPS reader Garmin, which is official ICTY GPS reader, and I don't know exactly what satellite was used, how many satellite was located in that moment. GPS was operated by ICTY investigator.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know whether the satellite used was a civilian or a military one?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I come now to the elaboration of this circular system. If I understood correctly, you have a tripod, a camera, an apparatus for taking photographs which has 20 positions, each time the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. axis being moved by 18 degrees. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Was the system entirely automatic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: The system is not completely automatic. There is no machine driving a photo camera. On the top of the tripod there is special head. On that head there is 20 holes which are 20 different angles. So each movement of that photo head is exact same. It's exactly ten degrees. Sorry. Eighteen, twenty. It's basically -- yes, it's 20, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think it would be 18 degrees, to be quite precise, mathematically, so -- is that right? Eighteen degrees. Because 20 times 20 gives us 400, but 20 times 18 is 360. Thank you. Yes. But the system is not automated, so it is you yourself who has to manipulate each time the position of the camera; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: That's true. And each time when I am moving the camera, it is moving exactly same angle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Could you tell this Chamber the average time needed to make these 20 changes of angles?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Between 2 minutes and 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when you change each time the angle or the axis of the shot, you sometimes had to regulate the focus as well as the lighting. And is this regulation done automatically?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: The lens was set on manual. First stop was usually 11, which will create a very deep field. And basically, it was operated with the remote control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Another question had to do with this field. Is it correct, Witness, that for the long distance planes, although the angle is always identical, that the fields may differ, depending on the distance of the object being visualised and filmed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, as a result of that, do we have the overlapping of photographs and of the images? Witness, who is going to choose the part of the photograph which will be retained to compose the circular image? Who does that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: The decision is done by computer, because programme is created in such way that from each negative is taking only middle part from a negative, and the left and right part will be overlapped with the next image. If I can explain, Your Honour, it looks like this: This is negative. Here is the centre part of image. Next image is coming like this to that one. I will not fold this. I will just leave it like this. And then it will come like this. The next one is coming in the absolutely same way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that the image that we finally see in realtime may have lasted about 10 minutes, which is the time necessary to make the full circle. I think that is what I gathered from your statement a moment ago. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, Witness, that we are showing in a static form something which, in time, may have lasted relatively a long time, several minutes?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: The time difference between first and last shot is only because we didn't want to have, for example, one car waiting for a street light, which is red, and then the last one, which is in the same spot, a blue. What we did in 10 minutes, we will wait until the conditions are like that that nothing is on the image which can be changed. Then quickly, we will make the whole rotation. So it means that waiting was basically to avoid any two different cars or two different pedestrians on the same shot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But my question referred to mobile objects. Because this photograph, using necessarily an "X" amount of time, mobile objects theoretically may be seen two or three times on the same static image. Is that correct, theoretically? In theory?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: No, because we are waiting them to leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I understand that. But in theory, if you were not careful, then theoretically we could have several times the same mobile object on a single photograph shown to us as an instant image?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes, theoretically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you quite certain of having redacted all type of animated object from this type of photograph?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for the clarity of your answer. Thank you very much. Witness, I now come to another aspect of this technique. We received in connection with your statement a certain number of photo images. I'm showing them to you from a distance. Can you recognise them as being those coming from your office, shall I call them? Shall I call them that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Show me. Yes, from this distance, I think it's from us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, just for the clarity of the record, from a distance, Defence counsel shows two or more pieces of paper which, from a distance, seems to contain small photographic pictures of something. Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in the interests of accuracy, I would be grateful if the witness had an opportunity to view those contact prints much closer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the problem is we can't just read a few lines of these pictures, so we can't use our normal technique; that is, to read to the witness exactly what is on these pieces of paper. So let me be clear: If it's just to say is this the kind of document you used or you had in your office, that's fine. If it comes any more precise, you have to either tender them into evidence or have them marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I simply wanted to place them on the ELMO, and we -- first, I wanted to make sure that this was the type of print shown by the witness. Now I can have them placed on the ELMO. The exhibit has a number, handwritten 20, and another series of number; 0106-1217.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if the witness recognises these as the -- as you call it "planche," do you intend to tender them into evidence? Do you have copies for the Bench and --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The problem is, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... I mean I do understand that, of course, it's not easy to prepare for the cross-examination. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The problem is when we copy this, it is highly illegible. It's only a technical problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, are we discussing prints that you, yourself, have made with your camera?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is it the type of print that were used for making photos at 360 degrees?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what kind of other prints were used -- I will provide another one to make things clearer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Usher, could you take this print, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just in order to be sure the Prosecution knows what these documents -- would you then, please, Mr. Usher, first -- the other one, at least show it to the Prosecution, and then give it to the Bench so that we have a better view.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I had no warning of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you think we can proceed meanwhile, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The other one can then -- oh, yes. Would you please put that on the ELMO, Mr. Usher. And please give the original, which is in the hands of the Prosecution now, to the Bench so that finally we also can have an idea of what it's all about. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This compact [as interpreted] print, is it the kind that is used for making such photos?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell us how many photos we have that appear on the print that you have on the screen? I think that they have been numbered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I thought that you had said that you made a rotation, 20 times 18, and that we should have only 20 pauses. How can you explain that difference, that gap?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: As you can see, there is a 21 shot, which is a horizontal, and the rest is vertical. Basically -- sorry, it was 21 vertical and 5 horizontal shots. And the first one and the number 21 is completely the same. So it makes from 1 to 20 is panoramic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we put another document, 211, 89. Could you put it on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In the meantime, Mr. President, might I have access to the photograph which is presently on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think it has been shown to you already. And after that, the Bench is also very much interested to see it. Could you please, Mr. Usher, put the other one on the ELMO. While Mr. Piletta-Zanin proceeds, the Bench could also see that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, here we have a number of photos that are either horizontal or vertical, whichever way you look at it. How many pauses are there on the print?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I didn't translate that.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: If you start looking them from number 1 to number 20, you will see that it's one continuation, that it's one full movement of 360.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that question was not translated. Perhaps my friend could repeat the question so it could be translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please translate -- could you repeat the question, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I do hear it in French, so I didn't notice.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you indicated there were 28 shots on the print, and I asked you how come we had 28 when we know that 20 are enough for a full rotation? And your answer was, could you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: Yes. The shots from number 1 to 20, that's from a same rotation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The photos that you were going to use were, in fact -- later on, were they selected, chosen?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: No. It's from one full rotation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here we have 28 photos that form a single rotation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN LESIC
utterances.text: No. There is 20 photos shot, from number 1 to 20. It's one full rotation. And as I can see, you can follow that step by step. The rest is just test.
